name: Lotus

tenures.finisher: the Sinner / the Lotus Pod (Realm 23, 18 January 2003: a 450 splash, "his very own finishing maneuver, the Sinner", and "his own finishing piledriver", the Lotus Pod)
tenures.source: the fed's own History of Lights Out Wrestling (captured 18 April 2003); the fed's own Realm card and Realm 23 (18 January 2003), Realm 29 (8 April 2003) and Shellshock (April 2003); the fed's own roster and Champions and Contenders pages of February 2003; the fed's own roleplay board (his roleplays of 11 to 19 April 2003); the fed's own front page of June 2004 and the 50th Realm (Hall of Fame)
tenures.note: The fed's own history page places him from its first weeks in mid-2002: "crowning champions such as Lotus in the Xtreme Division and CADE as the World Champion", then "Lotus ascending", a World title match against Mike Meyhu at Infinite, a reign the fed's own Shellshock commentary counts ("First there was CADE... Then Mike Meyhu... Then Lotus, Rich Sherwin, and Meyhu again") and the title lost to Rich Sherwin when CADE cost him it; at BattleCry he took Sean Dahmer "back with him... to the Nethervoid", and he "had returned" for the three-way World title main event at War Wounds. Neither reign has a dated row of its own in the surviving record. His last match is Shellshock (April 2003), where he beats Jesse Jamester for the number-one contendership and is shot dead in the ring at the show's end; the fed's own front page of June 2004 and its 50th Realm name him to LOW's Hall of Fame, and a roleplay of 2005 has Eric Russo trying to raise his corpse. His own card slot, superstars.cgi?lotus, survives only as an empty 2006 template.

identity.note: LOW's own pages bill two different Lotuses. The fed's own news of the Saikyo System's debut (front page, captured 12 June 2004) introduces Raizo Tenzan's partner as "his cousin, the 5'3 123 pound 'Kogeru Grrl' Lotus, not to be mistaken by LOW's own Lotus", a Japanese 17-year-old, and the same page names the other Lotus to LOW's Hall of Fame beside Mike Meyhu. The fed kept two card slots: superstars.cgi?lotus2 is hers (captured 7 July 2004: Fukuoka, 5'3", 123 lb, "she", "Lo", the 'S-Unit' and the 'Lotus Clutch', "I ain't got none yet... I just got here"), and superstars.cgi?lotus is the one the fed's own Retired and Hall of Fame roster pages link (captured 11 September and 13 December 2005; that card survives only as an empty template). Realm 23 (18 January 2003) stages the 2002-03 Lotus as "the black man" in a hooded coal-black cloak, a "former world champion" back from the Nethervoid, finishing with the Sinner (a 450 splash) and the Lotus Pod (a piledriver); Shellshock (April 2003) has him shot dead in the ring. She debuts with Raizo Tenzan on Realm 48 (12 April 2004), "Lotus, as she called herself", and on the 50th Realm the fed inducts Tristan Belmont where "only Lotus and Mike Meyhu" had gone while she wins the Tag Team titles on the same card. Every vital differs, and the fed itself says they are not the same.
Distinct pending a verdict: a shared generic name in other promotions, and nothing held names LOW's 2002-03 Lotus in any of them (a lead, not a finding).
